subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and if so should it be modeled as `tools.selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, a scoped allow entry, or folded into per-spawn `toolsAllow` work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and alters how tool-deny security boundaries flow from requester agents to subagents.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins semantics and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let the per-spawn tool restriction work own child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still needs separate profiles or instructions.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins semantics and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest available routing signal for a security-sensitive public config/API decision on this issue.
